schema.title: UpdateCredentialRequest
schema.description:
Send only the fields you want to change; anything you leave out is untouched, and omitted fields
are not validated.

To change the password, use the credential-rotation endpoint rather than this one.

UserName.description:
Rename the login. The old name is released and the new one must be free across the whole
service.

A name already in use returns `422`; a reserved name is rejected by validation with `400`.
Either way nothing changes. A credential that already holds a reserved name is exempt from
that check, so its other fields can still be updated.

Alias.description:
The label shown in the dashboard. Sending an empty string resets it to the login name rather
than clearing it.

Permission.description: What this credential may do with files. Takes effect on the next connection.

HomeDirectory.description:
Where the credential lands after connecting. Sending an empty string resets it to
`/home/{UserName}`. Must start with a forward slash and must not end with one.

ChrootDirectory.description: The highest directory this credential can reach. Sending an empty string resets it to `/`.

Email.description:
Where portal invitations and password resets are sent. Changing it clears the verified flag
until the new address is confirmed.

State.description:
Whether the credential can connect. Prefer the activate and deactivate endpoints, which say
what they do at the call site.

ExpiresAt.description:
When access should stop working, in Unix epoch milliseconds, or `null` to remove the expiry.
Must be at least a day away and no more than a year away.

Security.description: How the person using this credential proves who they are.

MFA.description:
Multi-factor authentication for web portal sign-in. It does not apply to SFTP, FTPS or S3
connections, which authenticate with a password or key.

Required.description: Whether the user must complete a second factor to sign in to the portal.

Factors.description: The second factors enrolled for this credential. Empty until one is added.

Type.description: The kind of factor, for example a time-based one-time password app.

IsPrimary.description: Whether this factor is offered first at sign-in.

Network.description: Where this credential is allowed to connect from.

InboundRules.description:
Network rules, evaluated in order, first match wins. An empty list means connections are
accepted from anywhere.

items.title: InboundRule
items.description:
One network rule controlling where a credential may connect from. Rules are evaluated in order,
and the first match wins.

Id.description: Identifier for the rule, unique within the credential.

Action.description: What to do with a connection that matches this rule.

Protocol.description: Which protocol the rule applies to. Use `all` to cover every protocol.

Source.description:
Where the connection comes from: a single IPv4 or IPv6 address, or a CIDR range such as
`203.0.113.0/24`.

Description.description: A note explaining why the rule exists. Shown in the dashboard.

State.description: Whether the rule is currently in effect.

network.summary: Restrict where the credential may connect from
